reason: I fetched the named page, the John Milton Reading Room at Dartmouth, and it states the text is From Poems (1673) and numbers the sonnet 19, exactly as the corrected card says. The transcription runs: line 11 Bear his milde yoak, they serve him best, his State; line 12 Is Kingly. Thousands at his bidding speed; line 13 And post o're Land and Ocean without rest:; line 14 They also serve who only stand and waite. So the old spellings o're and waite are the 1673 readings, the colon after rest is right, the capitals Land and Ocean are right, the closing full stop is right, and the locator lines 12 to 14 is right. The correction the verifier made was the real one: the modernised over and wait belong to later editions, and the card no longer claims Beeching's Oxford text. Attribution is not in dispute, the sonnet is untitled in 1673 so citing it by first line is correct and avoids the Newton title On His Blindness of 1752, and the card's note already says the sonnet is numbered 19 in modern editions rather than asserting a 1673 number. No misattribution trap applies. shipped.js returns no match, no near match, Milton at 0 of 3, not banned. Scope clean, 1673, no scripture despite the religious cast of the sonnet, publishable, and it is the month's own line: they also serve who only stand and wait is stillness itself and is consoling rather than bleak at six in the morning. Poetry is the form. The source line leads with the name, carries no dash, and runs 79 characters. One defect I could not turn into a refutation but the editor should fix: the quotation opens mid line, since line 12 is Is Kingly. Thousands at his bidding speed, so the card prints as its first verse line something that is not a line of the sonnet. Rule 7 asks for the lineation of the edition named. The capital on Thousands is authentic, because it follows a full stop, and the note discloses the truncation plainly, so the card is honest rather than wrong; but the house precedent in this year was to move a quotation start back to a line head, as was done for Marianne Moore at 07-poet-06. Either start at Is Kingly, or say in the locator that the quotation begins inside line 12, as my betterCitation does.
